request.subject: Can Wolves Really Change Rivers? - part 3: Wolves Did Not Do It Alone
request.title: Can Wolves Really Change Rivers? (Part 3/3)
request.description:
Wolves got the credit for healing Yellowstone, but scientists say bears, hunters, water and beavers played big roles too. Did you believe the viral video?

Part 3 of 3: Can Wolves Really Change Rivers?

Sources:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_wolves_in_Yellowstone
https://www.nps.gov/articles/the-big-scientific-debate-trophic-cascades.htm
https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/apr/07/yellowstone-research-reignites-debate-over-wolf-ge/

Stock footage: Pexels. Made with AI-assisted narration.

#shorts #truestory

extra_params.video_script: The famous claim that wolves changed rivers has a big problem. In Part 2, elk numbers fell and willows grew after wolves returned. But cougars, bears and hunters outside the park were killing elk too. Later studies found the willow gains were smaller and patchier than claimed. In dry spots, willows barely grew, even with fewer elk around. Water, and the beavers that hold it back, mattered too. Many streams changed so much without beavers that they haven't bounced back. Wolves changed Yellowstone. They just didn't do it alone. Subscribe for a new true story every day.
